claims.text: The starting material is a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments in a Cu matrix.
Optimizing W particle or ligament size and distribution can produce a hierarchical microstructure.
The optimized hierarchical microstructure will minimize phase separation in W–Cu.
The optimized hierarchical microstructure will minimize interfacial void formation in W–Cu.
Minimizing phase separation and interfacial voids will improve thermal conductivity.
The optimized W–Cu composite will have higher thermal conductivity than an untreated W–Cu composite.
The predicted conductivity improvement applies under heat-transfer conditions relevant to W-based plasma-facing-material/Cu-based cooling-component joints.
The predicted conductivity improvement applies under irradiation conditions relevant to W-based plasma-facing-material/Cu-based cooling-component joints.
Other microstructural features may affect the thermal conductivity.
Failure of the optimized composite to achieve a 10% conductivity increase with p < 0.05 relative to the unoptimized control would falsify the hypothesis.
